clue.text: "Pass him, anyway" — how accidents result

indicators.note: any way at all means the letters of the quoted words may be put in any order

explanation.surface: A driver's reckless 'Pass him, anyway' is what leads to crashes on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is the anagram signal: PASSHIM rearranged makes the answer; 'how ... result' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps are unlucky mischances, the same thing as minor accidents.

clue.text: Rough, long-haired dog taken out for a breather?

definitions.text: Rough, long-haired dog taken out for a breather?

parts.words: Rough, long-haired dog taken out for a breather?
parts.note: reads like a shaggy pet walked for air, but describes a device taken out of the pocket by someone rough of breath

explanation.definitionFit: An asthmatic, breathing roughly, takes out this medical device to breathe in its drug.

clue.text: He gets put out and angry

indicators.note: out signals that the word put is jumbled

explanation.surface: A man is annoyed and cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is only a link; 'put out' reads as annoyed, matching the definition, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is a colloquial expression meaning agitated or worked up.

clue.text: Correct to accept son is to succeed

indicators.note: to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: proper means correct or right
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Doing the right thing by taking in a son brings success.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, much like succeeding.

clue.text: Bill gives way and agrees

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
to cede is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation is passed after its opponents yield and consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a law or a person's name; here it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or assent to it.

clue.text: Scholar's in the money in this part of a foreign city

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: cash is money
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An academic is rich in a North African quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the old walled citadel quarter of a North African city.

clue.text: Active great-niece lacking first aid gets upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means one letter is taken away from the relative
first takes the opening letter of the word aid

explanation.surface: A lively young relative is distressed at not getting help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking first aid' removes A from GREATNIECE, leaving GRETNIECE, which 'gets upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means full of vigour and activity.

clue.text: Ran out of time

parts.note: reads like a deadline missed, but means a life or a term that came to its close

explanation.definitionFit: A licence or a life that has come to an end has lapsed, its time over.

clue.text: A boxer normally has one, even if not hungry

definitions.text: A boxer normally has one, even if not hungry

parts.words: A boxer normally has one, even if not hungry
parts.note: a boxer's corner man, the second, helps in the ring, while the phrase also means another plateful at dinner

explanation.definitionFit: An extra serving of food at a meal; a boxer's second gives help in the corner.

clue.text: Pass for a mere youngster

definitions.meaning: a note or voucher permitting entry or credit
an impudent young girl or child

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a signed voucher or note and a pert young person.

clue.text: Fails to turn out as intended

definitions.text: Fails to turn out as intended

parts.words: Fails to turn out as intended
parts.note: reads like a plan going wrong, but means someone failing to get out of bed at the planned hour

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays asleep past the alarm does not turn out of bed when intended.

clue.text: Recalling students is a blunder

indicators.note: calling back suggests reading the word for students from the end to the start

parts.note: pupils are school students

explanation.surface: A teacher calling pupils back to class makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal name for a careless mistake or error.

clue.text: A hothouse for Protestant extremists?

parts.note: a glasshouse for citrus trees whimsically pictured as housing Orangemen, members of the Protestant Orange Order of Northern Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: This is a greenhouse built for growing citrus trees, which suggests a home for Orangemen.

clue.text: Uninterrupted flow of traffic

parts.note: suggests cars moving freely on a road, but traffic here means commerce crossing borders without tariffs

explanation.definitionFit: Commerce between nations without duties or barriers lets goods move unhindered.

clue.text: Outdo others with fast time — fantastic!

indicators.note: one piece is joined to the other

parts.note: to excel is to surpass others
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Running a quick lap and beating rivals is superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast time' suggests a quick race time; it means the period of fasting, LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and fantastic both mean extremely good.

clue.text: Outstanding bosses for the stables

definitions.meaning: raised knobs or bosses that stand out from a surface
establishments where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: Prominent managers are suited to running horse yards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both projecting knobs on a surface and horse-breeding establishments.

clue.text: Coal left in fire

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: A lump of coal is left burning in the grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a blaze for the coal, but it means dismiss, SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack is the name for small pieces and dust of coal.

clue.text: One having a desire to accept university chair

indicators.note: to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a longer is one who longs or yearns

explanation.surface: An aspiring academic wants to take a professorial post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' looks like a professorship, given 'university', but it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining seat for relaxing, a kind of chair.

clue.text: Yard chase forged money

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: In a Scotland Yard pursuit, counterfeit notes are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters; 'forged' rearranges YARDCHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready cash is money immediately available in hand.

clue.text: Plans a football pool's entry that's a winner

definitions.meaning: drafts or prepares, as a document

definitions.text: a football pool's entry that's a winner
definitions.meaning: on the British football pools, betting on drawn matches, score draws coming up pay out

explanation.surface: Someone draws up plans for a winning football pools coupon.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results, in which predicted draws were the prized outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw up is to draft a plan; draws coming up wins on the pools.

clue.text: Sort of roll made with herb and an American stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing means one piece is filled with the other

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
USA, the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A bread roll is made with herb stuffing in American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' looks like the herb-and-onion filling of a roast; it is the container signal. A sausage roll is a British pastry snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage roll is a British snack of sausage meat in pastry.

clue.text: Half turn to the church and the sound of bells

indicators.note: one piece is attached to the other

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: turn means the word is read backwards

parts.note: semi is the prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Partway round, bells ring out from the church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses SEMI to IMES, which joins CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimes are the tuned ringing tones of a set of bells.

clue.text: Nick goes after speculator to give a heavy beating

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other in the answer

parts.note: a bull is a stock market speculator betting on rising prices
to nick and to whip are both slang for steal

explanation.surface: A thief named Nick follows a dealer and assaults him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the slang verb for steal, WHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To bullwhip someone is to flog them with a long heavy lash.

clue.text: Maximum effort at the end of the innings

definitions.text: at the end of the innings
definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side whose batsmen are all dismissed

explanation.surface: A batting side gives everything until its innings closes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings ends when ten batsmen are dismissed and the side is declared all out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means total exertion and also a cricket team dismissed entirely.

clue.text: The student has a place in Tibet

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A student owns a spot in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Mere agents may make them

indicators.note: suggests the letters can be made into something else by reworking them

explanation.surface: Even humble go-betweens can broker deals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging MEREAGENTS makes the answer, and agents do make deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents negotiate deals and contracts, which are formal accords between parties.

clue.text: A course taken abroad

parts.note: a way is a route or course

explanation.surface: Someone takes a course overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away means being absent, as when travelling overseas.

clue.text: Object is to get a tiresome person to admit corruption

indicators.note: to let in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pest is an annoying nuisance
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A nuisance is made to confess to bribery and objects.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection, the verb sense of object.

clue.text: Garments appear dishevelled on student

indicators.note: one piece follows the other in a down-style placing
messed up and untidy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: Clothes look scruffy on a young learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' looks like it describes untidy clothes; it is the anagram signal, and L, the learner plate, comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing.
